TightFromBlockedRun

a run of blocked numbers makes a tight lonely runner
Proved in Leanring 2The Lonely Runner: pile-ups, shifts and residue sieves

The consecutive speeds 1 up to one less than the number of runners are tight: the time one over the number of runners gives every runner one part of a lap of room, and no time gives more (Dirichlet's pigeonhole). Speed up the runner of speed r to m times its speed. If every number from the number of runners minus r up to m times that, minus one, shares a factor with r (a run of positions blocked by the wheels of r), the new set is still tight. The proof replaces one runner at a time (Goddyn and Wong's Lemma 3.2): at a time when only the sped-up runner could have been close, either a smaller wheel of r takes its place, or an unchanged runner whose speed is the inverse remainder for r does, and the blocked run is exactly what keeps that runner unchanged. A blocked run is shorter than the speed that blocks it, which keeps the sped-up runner off the fence post at the time one over the number of runners. This is the wheel-native part of the link between tight lonely runners and Jacobsthal's problem (JacobsthalTightness): the longer the blocked runs of a wheel cycle, the more a runner can be sped up. Goddyn and Wong 2006, Theorem 2.1 (sufficiency direction) and Lemma 3.2, at times that are fractions; never strictly lonely means every fractional time has a runner at most one part from the start. Not proved: the necessity direction, the several-runner Theorem 3.1, and real times.

consecutive_covered
proved in Lean
The consecutive speeds are never strictly lonely: at every fractional time one of them is at most one part of a lap from the start (Dirichlet).
/-- **The consecutive speeds are never strictly lonely** (Dirichlet). -/
def consecutive_covered : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → never_strictly_lonely n (Finset.Icc (1 : ℤ) ((n : ℤ) - 1))

one_step_replacement
proved in Lean
Replacing one speed r by m times it keeps a set never strictly lonely, if the wheels of r and the inverse remainders for r are covered by unchanged speeds in the right range (Goddyn and Wong, Lemma 3.2).
/-- **One-step replacement** (Goddyn and Wong, Lemma 3.2). If a speed set is
never strictly lonely, then so is the set with `r` replaced by `m * r`,
provided each `r / p` (for a prime wheel `p` of `r`) is in the new set, and each
remainder `q` sharing no factor with `r` is the remainder of some speed of the
new set between `m * (n - r)` and `n + r`. -/
def one_step_replacement : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (X : Finset ℤ) (r m : ℤ), 2 ≤ n → 1 ≤ r → r ≤ n → 2 ≤ m →
    never_strictly_lonely n X →
    (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → (p : ℤ) ∣ r → r / p ∈ insert (m * r) (X.erase r)) →
    (∀ q : ℤ, IsCoprime q r → ∃ b ∈ insert (m * r) (X.erase r),
      m * (n - r) ≤ b ∧ b ≤ n + r ∧ r ∣ b - q) →
    never_strictly_lonely n (insert (m * r) (X.erase r))
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

blocked_run_short
proved in Lean
A run of numbers all sharing a factor with r is shorter than r.
/-- **A blocked run is shorter than the speed blocking it**: any `r` consecutive
numbers include one leaving remainder 1 for `r`. -/
def blocked_run_short : Prop :=
  ∀ r lo hi : ℤ, 1 ≤ r → blocked_run r lo hi → hi - lo + 1 ≤ r - 1
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

single_acceleration_tight
proved in Lean
If the numbers from (number of runners minus r) to m times that, minus one, are all blocked by the wheels of r, the consecutive speeds with r sped up to m times r are tight: lonely at one over the number of runners and never strictly lonely.
/-- **A blocked run gives a tight set** (Goddyn and Wong, Theorem 2.1,
sufficiency). If the numbers from `n - r` to `m * (n - r) - 1` are all blocked by
the wheels of `r`, then the consecutive speeds with `r` sped up to `m * r` are
`n - 1` distinct speeds, lonely at the time `1 / n`, and never strictly lonely. -/
def single_acceleration_tight : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (r m : ℤ), 2 ≤ n → 1 ≤ r → r ≤ (n : ℤ) - 1 → 2 ≤ m →
    blocked_run r ((n : ℤ) - r) (m * ((n : ℤ) - r) - 1) →
    (accelerated n r m).card = n - 1 ∧ lonely_at (accelerated n r m) n 1 ∧
      never_strictly_lonely n (accelerated n r m)
